text.p: Israel opened a new page on Tuesday in its internationally condemned campaign to expand Jewish settlements in the West Bank and Gaza, offering in a newspaper advertisement 120 houses for sale in 30 outposts.
The sale drew immediate Arab anger, two days before Prime Minister Benjamim Netanyahu's planned summit with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat at the Erez crossing between Israel and Gaza.

A Housing Ministry spokesman said the dwellings were the first of some 3,000 empty homes which the government decided last October to sell to the public as part of its policy to widen existing settlements.

He said it was the first time the ministry had taken out such an advertisement since Netanyahu came to power in June pledging to sink Israeli roots deeper in land captured from the Arabs in the 1967 Middle East war.
"A large number of houses needed renovation and about 120 have now been freed up (for sale)," the spokesman said.

Israel's previous Labour-led government froze the sale of the 3,000 units, in small settlements deep inside the West Bank and Gaza where Labour was unlikely to demand a permanent foothold in a final peace agreement with the PLO.
"This shows that the Israeli government is not serious about peace," Ahmed Abdel-Rahman, secretary of the Palestinian Authority, said of the advertisement.
"The attempt to nurture settlements, by expanding them or encouraging settlers to move in, will not make these artificial structures remain on Palestinian land," he told Reuters.
The full-page advertisement in the mass-circulation Maariv newspaper evoked memories of settlement campaigns launched in the 1980s by previous Likud administrations.
"You can build on this ad," it said, listing the names and telephone numbers of 30 settlements in which the ministry said private homes were available.

A telephone call to one of the outposts, Kedim, nestled in a pine forest near the self-ruled town of Jenin in the West Bank, elicited a bargain price of $54,000 for a 128 square-metre (1,376 sq-ft) home with a small yard.
A similarly sized home in central Israel would sell for at least $300,000.
"We have one double apartment left and 30 flats of 60 square metres (645 sq ft) priced at $43,000," a Kedim official said.

The PLO has called Israel's settlement policy, which includes tax breaks and other financial benefits for Israelis living in the West Bank, Gaza and Golan Heights, a violation of its peace deals with the Jewish state.
Israel's main ally, the United States, and many other countries have described the outposts as obstacles to peace.

The ministry spokesman said that in addition to the 3,000 empty homes, the ministry had finalised a previously announced plan to market land in the West Bank and Gaza for private-sector construction this year of some 5,000 housing units.
He stressed that none of the plans envisaged construction outside of existing settlements.
"We do not think all 5,000 will be sold but estimate the number will be around 3,000," the spokesman said.
The plan, he said, was in line with government decisions and had been approved by Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai, whose permission is needed for construction in settlements.
More than 130,000 Jews live in settlements scattered among some two million Arabs in the West Bank and Gaza, areas captured in the 1967 war.
